name: Empty Space Caching with Bit Vector E
definition: A fine-granular empty space skipping mechanism using a bit vector $E$ to mark invisible regions. It stores one bit per $2^3$ voxels (an 'empty block') on the finest LOD. If all voxels in a block have invisible labels, the bit is set to 1. This reduces memory usage from 64 bits per invisible voxel (in hash table M) to 1/8 bits per voxel for invisible blocks.
summary: Empty Space Caching with Bit Vector E is a fine-granular optimization that uses a compact bit vector to skip hash lookups for entire blocks of invisible voxels, reducing memory pressure and lookup latency.
